editorial:
Imagine you are dealing with the loss of a parent, but then you start noticing things that just do not add up. That is exactly where you start with this gritty crime story. You follow a grieving son who is convinced his mother did not just die from her illness in a Stockholm hospital. He believes something much darker happened behind closed doors. You get to join the steady and smart Detective Beck as he digs into the hospital's secrets. The vibe is very cold and serious, making you feel the tension of a medical cover-up where the people in charge are trying to hide the truth at all costs.

What really works here is the slow build-up and the realistic acting. It does not rely on huge explosions, but rather on the mystery of who is lying. Some parts might feel a bit slow if you want constant action, but the payoff is worth it. If you love a good puzzle, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: You find out that the death was not natural at all. A doctor had been playing god and making mistakes with patient care. The twist reveals that the mother was actually killed to cover up medical errors and greed within the hospital system. Detective Beck eventually finds the proof needed to take down the corrupt staff. The movie wraps up with the son finally getting the justice he wanted and the killers facing the law.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves medical mysteries and police procedurals.
